general.statement: The collected works of an artist and designer building practical systems and curious artifacts.
general.about:
My professional practice spans across digital product, brand identity, and art direction. For over a decade, I’ve contributed my work to organizations of all sizes. Currently, as part of [recidiviz](https://www.recidiviz.org/), I design catalytic systems that actively reduce the amount of people incarcerated in the U.S.

Outside of my career, you’ll find me reading esoteric essays, tinkering with cameras, or practicing Muay Thai. I spent my childhood in the Caribbean and my adolescence in California so I find rainy days beautifully nostalgic but cold winters really \**** me.

projects.heading: Civic Impact
projects.description: Digital products aimed at systemic criminal justice issues in order to reduce the amount of people incarcerated in the U.S. Since 2019, I've worked on the product strategy, brand ethos, digital design system, website, and team operations.
projects.title: Civic Impact
projects.credits: Sonia Chokshi, Ian MacFarland, Allison Chan, William DeShazer

projects.description: Logo and brand work for a community made up of students, educators, writers, engineers, historians, activists, and scientists – all coming together to reimagine techno-optimism for a better collective future.
projects.title: Tech Journal

projects.description: Logo explorations for a venture capital studio based in New Mexico.

projects.heading: Justice System
projects.description: As part of a national initiative to enhance the consistency and transparency of data in the criminal justice system, our goal was to build a platform for gathering essential data from criminal justice agencies across the nation and get them into the hands of policymakers to support more informed decision-making.
projects.title: Justice System

projects.heading: Better Reading
projects.description: Concepts for [Matter](https://hq.getmatter.com), a reading tool that chooses agency over algorithm and quality over recency. Anchored to the onboarding experience, the design harmonized typography with minimal illustrations to guide the user along core functionality while conveying the tool's values.

projects.heading: Pandemic Response
projects.description: Digital product design for a set of tools that correctional workers used to track and anticipate the impact of Covid-19 inside of prison facilities. Used in all 50 states, the toolkit allowed users to: 1) project cases, hospitalizations, and deaths among both staff and the incarcerated population, 2) compare before-and-after scenarios for policy changes and early release decisions and, 3) model the current rate of spread and trajectory of the outbreak in each facility.
projects.title: Pandemic Response
projects.credits: C. Andrew Warren, Clementine Jacoby, Joshua Essex

projects.heading: Emotional Health
projects.description:
Digital product and brand identity design for a wellness platform. Conceived as an iOS app, the audio-first anonymous community focused on mental health and emotional support.

Inline with its values, the harmful “endless feed” of information was omitted by design. The ephemeral content that took its place emphasized accessibility to marginalized people, especially the visually impaired. Service was supported for 2 years before shutting down in 2022.
projects.title: Emotional Health

projects.title: Aerospace

projects.heading: City Planner
projects.description: To create a balanced environment for local residents, we designed an open-source and free-to-use platform that leveraged publicly available data to inform city planners, investment firms, and activists alike.
projects.title: City Planner

projects.heading: Smart Cities
projects.description: As part of a larger 'smart cities' initiative, this was an experiment to use real world rewards to incentivize alternate modes of transportation for daily commuters.
projects.title: Smart Cities

projects.heading: Waze
projects.description: Changing the way the world moves through everyday acts of cooperation. I was the lead designer across all growth initiatives where we raised the monthly active users from 55M to 110M and formed partnerships with local agencies internationally. Archival of further work in progress.
projects.title: Waze
projects.credits: Haraldur Thorleifsson, Dominic Flask, Robin Noguier

projects.heading: Disaster Relief
projects.description: Following hurricane Maria, my brother and I embarked on a mission to raise $10k worth of relief and personally deliver over 350 industrial-grade water filters. The journey took us across 10 of the most impacted towns in Puerto Rico as we formed partnerships with on-site military units, World Central Kitchen, The Home Depot, and Sam's Club. We named the project Clean Water Fund.
projects.title: Disaster Relief
